CHIEF COMPLAINT
Suspected kidney stone, hypertension, and diabetes management.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient Angela presents with a history of recurrent kidney stones, approximately 7 to 8 episodes. She reports pain that has been up and down, prompting an emergency room visit last week. She believes she passed the current stone approximately 3 days ago. She denies current hematuria and denies current pain. At the hospital, she was given Percocet for pain management. She has not seen a urologist in approximately one year. Regarding hypertension, blood pressure at today's visit was 150/90. Patient reports taking a blood pressure cuff at home 2 to 3 times per week with readings typically between 130-140 systolic and 60-70 diastolic. Patient attributes higher office readings to possible white coat syndrome. Regarding diabetes, patient reports not checking blood sugars frequently but states they seem to be doing pretty well. Patient also mentions previous issues with insomnia, currently experiencing occasional difficulty sleeping due to worry, which is somewhat relieved by meditation apps. Patient has tried melatonin previously without significant benefit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain. Patient denies abdominal pain. Patient denies current hematuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Recurrent kidney stones (approximately 7-8 episodes)
Hypertension
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
Insomnia
Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (previously known)

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports frequent consumption of fast food, cakes, and cookies, with difficulty reducing intake due to on-the-go lifestyle and limited time for food preparation. Patient sleeps with television on and keeps phone at bedside. Patient has tried meditation apps which help with insomnia.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood Pressure: 150/90 mmHg
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles
Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur, previously known, no worsening
Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation
Costovertebral Angle: No tenderness to palpation bilaterally

RESULTS
A1C: 6.7 (from recent visit, down from initial diagnosis one year ago)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Recurrent Kidney Stones: Patient has passed the current stone. Plan to obtain urinalysis and urine culture. Referral to urology with Dr. Harris for management of recurrent kidney stones.
Hypertension: Currently controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg. Continue current medication without changes. Continue refills through pharmacy.
Type 2 Diabetes: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Instructed patient to monitor blood glucose before meals.
Nutrition: Referral to nutrition consult to assist with diet modification, target sodium intake less than 2300 mg per day.
Insomnia: Start melatonin 10 mg as needed. Reinforce proper sleep hygiene including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool.
Follow-up: Return visit in 3 months.
